 EPF treads cautiously towards higher dividends
 By LYDIA NATHAN 
 Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026
 share 
 bookmark

 PETALING JAYA: Despite recording a jump in income investment for the first nine months of 2026 (9M26), there is no guarantee that the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) will be able to post higher figures for the full year.
 Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid told StarBiz that this was due to increased market volatility, particularly in regards to artificial intelligence (AI)-related counters and technology companies.
 “We will need to see how the EPF can navigate these challenges and set reasonable targets for its 2026 dividends, taking into consideration the market conditions.
 “But given its track record, it should be able to position itself to deliver respectable dividends for members,” he said.
 “The recent rise in gross investment income shows that the EPF is competent in managing the fund despite market volatility, whereby shock arising from the war in Iran still ongoing and oil prices remaining elevated,” he explained.
 Mohd Afzanizam also said that the share prices of AI-related counters had been affected by concerns over stock valuations.
 This, he said, included the recent kerfuffle involving Nvidia Corp, which also suggested a challenging road ahead.
 Nevertheless, the EPF still managed to deliver respectable gains. Mohd Afzanizam encouraged EPF members to keep their savings with the retirement fund, given its track record of good dividend payouts.
 Tradeview Capital chief executive officer Ng Zhu Hann said the fund’s performance was very much in line with global markets, which had a strong first half of financial year 2026, followed by a moderation in the 3Q26 and a worsening outlook in the 4Q26.
 Ng expects these developments to average out in the EPF’s performance for the full year.
 “But there is not much concern for now because the EPF’s Strategic Asset Allocation has focused on diversifying risk across asset classes and geographical locations.
 “I believe the EPF has what it takes to deliver a full-year performance for financial year 2026 (FY26) on par with FY25,” he opined.
 With a month and a half to go, Ng said it is important for the EPF to remain cautious and prudent in its investments, both locally and abroad. “If they can maintain this prudence towards the end of the year, there is a good chance the dividend for next year will be at least on par with that of 2025.”
 Meanwhile, the EPF’s total investment income for the 9M26 jumped 30% to RM83.32bil, compared with RM63.99bil for the same period a year ago. Voluntary contributions rose to RM18.27bil, reflecting continued interest among members in building additional retirement savings beyond mandatory contributions.
 In a statement, EPF chief executive officer Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn said he expected the trend to continue into the next quarter amid weaknesses in global stock markets and rising yields in the bond markets.
 However, the EPF’s investment income growth for the 3Q26, moderated to 3% from the same quarter a year ago.
 The retirement fund said total investment income for the quarter stood at RM25.82bil, compared with RM25.07bil in the corresponding period last year.
 For the quarter, income from equities increased 3% to RM17.41bil, supported by healthy global equity markets, which enabled the EPF’s fund managers to manage the portfolio and generate value.
 Fixed income instruments, comprising Malaysian Government Securities and equivalents, as well as loans and bonds, contributed RM7.12bil for the quarter.
 Total investment assets stood at RM1.55 trillion, with 38% invested globally.
